text: Building the Driftwood Media platform was the hard part. Presenting it well in an interview is a separate skill, and the same five-beat structure this catalog's AWS Capstone teaches applies here, built around what you actually have: a Snowflake, dbt, Airflow, Power BI platform.

The arc: the business problem -- subscriber numbers scattered across three systems. The architecture -- Snowflake to dbt to Airflow to Power BI. The build -- real models, a real DAG, real DAX measures. Production practices -- RBAC, masking, CI/CD, Terraform, resource monitors, Time Travel. And results -- one trusted number, refreshed daily, zero manual spreadsheet work. Most candidates stop at step three; steps four and five are what show you'd survive on a real data team.

Show live, if you can: the Power BI dashboard itself -- it's immediately legible to a non-technical interviewer, and it's the actual deliverable leadership asked for. Describe from a diagram instead: the full Airflow DAG graph, the dbt lineage graph, and the Terraform plan output -- dense, easy to misread quickly on a shared screen.

What would you do differently at scale has honest, specific answers named along the way: move ingestion from batch COPY INTO to Snowpipe if freshness requirements tightened. Resize the ETL warehouse first if the daily transform started taking longer. Increase the one-day Time Travel retention, understanding the storage-cost trade-off.
Final lesson: portfolio and interview prep -- what to actually put in front of a hiring manager.
